# vue-loader [![Build Status](https://example.invalid/gh/vuejs/vue-loader/tree/master.svg?style=shield)](https://example.invalid/gh/vuejs/vue-loader/tree/master) [![Windows Build status](https://example.invalid/api/projects/status/8cdonrkbg6m4k1tm/branch/master?svg=true)](https://example.invalid/project/yyx990803/vue-loader/branch/master) [![npm package](https://example.invalid/npm/v/vue-loader.svg?maxAge=2592000)](https://example.invalid/package/vue-loader)

> Vue.js component loader for [Webpack](https://example.invalid/).

<p align="center">
  <img width="809px" src="https://example.invalid/vuejs/vue-syntax-highlight/master/samples/screenshot.png">
</p>

The best way to get started is with [vue-cli](https://example.invalid/vuejs/vue-cli):

``` js
npm install -g vue-cli
vue init webpack-simple hello
cd hello
npm install
npm run dev
```

This will setup a basic Webpack + `vue-loader` project for you, with `*.vue` files and hot-reloading working out of the box!

For advanced `vue-loader` configuration, checkout the [documentation](https://example.invalid).
